vision: A coastal city lives on maps drawn by the Cartographers Guild. Every accurate map erases one memory from the person who supplied the survey. A young surveyor discovers that the Guild is using the city founding archive to make a perfect map that will erase the shared memory of a massacre. She must choose between a truthful map that frees the city from a comforting lie and a merciful map that preserves belonging. Intended experience: wonder at the strangeness of the coast, mounting dread as the cost becomes personal, and earned hope about chosen remembrance. Genre: a literary mystery with fantasy and horror passages. No explicit violence on the page; the tone is intimate and reflective, not grimdark. Themes: memory, complicity, and the ethics of knowledge.
